content.text: {"conditions":{"rc1":{"status":"gap","note":"The FAD conclusions (e.g., Complainant 'did not demonstrate at the interview that he was more qualified' than selectees, or that rating 'was fair') are stated without the underlying interview scores, qualifications comparison, or evidence that would let a reviewer trace evidence to conclusion."},"rc2":{"status":"review","note":"The 28 incidents are attributed to Complainant's claims and the ROI is mentioned, but the agency's findings (management's legitimate reasons, Colonel 1 and former supervisor agreeing the rating was fair) are not tied to identified affidavits, documents, or ROI exhibits."},"rc3":{"status":"review","note":"Individual incidents carry specific dates from April 2017 to June 2018, but the summary has no complaint filing, acceptance, ROI, or FAD dates, and the claim numbering is inconsistent (e.g., B17 and B7 references do not match the listed claims B17 and B6)."},"rc4":{"status":"gap","note":"The record names no FAD author or reviewer, and no criteria beyond a generic McDonnell Douglas framework and severe-or-pervasive standard; there is no sign that Complainant's responses to the ROI were considered before the FAD, and the decision addresses only some of the 28 incidents."},"rc5":{"status":"gap","note":"Because evidence-to-conclusion links, source attribution, and decision-process documentation are weak and most claims go unaddressed, an independent reviewer could not assess from this record alone whether the no-discrimination finding is supported."}}}
